an5.18:1.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing five qualities, a bhikkhu is practicing for the welfare of others but not for his own welfare.
an5.18:1.3: (1) Here, a bhikkhu is not accomplished in virtuous behavior himself but he encourages others to become accomplished in virtuous behavior;
an5.18:1.4: (2) he is not accomplished in concentration himself but he encourages others to become accomplished in concentration;
an5.18:1.5: (3) he is not accomplished in wisdom himself but he encourages others to become accomplished in wisdom;
an5.18:1.6: (4) he is not accomplished in liberation himself but he encourages others to become accomplished in liberation;
an5.18:1.7: (5) he is not accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation himself but he encourages others to become accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation.
an5.18:1.8: Possessing these five qualities, a bhikkhu is practicing for the welfare of others but not for his own welfare.”
